seo.title: Active Navigation — the moment someone searches to decide | Advia
seo.description: There are two ways to navigate. In one, the algorithm chooses for you; in the other, you search to decide, and there a brand can be the answer.

hero.lede: In one, consumers are entertained and the algorithm chooses for them. In the other they have a specific question, and there is an answer that helps them: become that answer and capitalise on Active Navigation.

pasiva.label: Passive navigation
pasiva.descripcion: Someone scrolls through content on their phone, in black and white, without looking for anything: the content just arrives and answers no question.

activa.label: Active Navigation
activa.descripcion: The same scene in colour: the questions of a single decision appear over the phone —“Best car in 2026” on Google, “BYD Seal VS Tesla Model S” on YouTube, “What car should I buy?” on ChatGPT—.

recorrido.lede: To find that answer, consumers ask themselves questions that lead them to consult different information channels. Our job is to make sure you are present in all of them.
recorrido.nota: A 35-year-old woman wants to switch to a more efficient car.
recorrido.door: This is how Vera draws this journey

util.titular: For advertising to be useful to a brand, it first has to be useful to its <key>consumer</key>
util.lede: Capitalising on Active Navigation positions you as the answer consumers need.
util.citaFuente: Blog · Introduction to Active Navigation, I
util.cita: “Advertising stops being advertising and becomes part of the <key>content</key>.”
